_comment: CLA-76's all-buttons SLOPE SHAPE — the output of `npm run fet:allshape` over
four stairs-fine.wav captures at 96 kHz, kept because the captures are licensed
audio and cannot be. Companion to cla76_stairs_fits.json; same reasons.
⚠ THE X AXIS ORIGIN IS ARBITRARY AND THAT IS NOT A DEFECT. Overshoot is
`level + drive - (THRESHOLD - drop)`, and drive and drop are exactly degenerate,
so absolute overshoot is unrecoverable from a staircase. The SHAPE is not: the
four captures are four windows onto one law, and the offsets that collapse them
are real. `cla76_stairsfine_rALL_I2.wav` is pinned at zero. Nothing downstream
may read an absolute overshoot off `curve[].shiftedLevelDb`.
⚠ THE CURVE IS DECIMATED — the extractor merges ~66 points and prints every
fifth. The collapse residual, the point counts and the span below are computed
on ALL the points, not on the 14 recorded here.
⚠ THE KNEE IS KEPT IN THIS CURVE (minGrDb 0), unlike the span, which is read
clear of the 7 dB guard. The rising left limb IS the bend, which is what makes
the knee width fittable from this table at all.
⚠ IT IS THE LAW CONVOLVED WITH THE ATTACK, like every staircase reading here.
Compare it only against our own kernel run through the identical extractor —
`ours` below is that control, recorded at the same time.
⚠ ATTACK DIAL 1 (the old protocol). CLA-76 is attack-invariant on this test, so
these are not attack-biased; our side at dial 1 is.
The control: our kernel through the identical extractor, as it read at the
time of the capture — the OLD ALL_RATIO_* family, before the incremental law
replaced it. Kept as the 'before' picture; it spans 0.9473 to 0.9521, i.e. it
is flat where the reference falls by 0.11.
